request.query: checkout-service memory keeps climbing; investigate metrics and logs

report.summary: During the requested 180-minute investigation window, checkout-service resident memory rose 1.2x, from 1257.56MiB to 1474.92MiB. Logs show heap usage at 92% with GC overhead warnings and five Java heap-space errors. These observations support heap exhaustion, but do not identify why heap utilization increased. A targeted OutOfMemoryError search returned zero matches, while the broader ERROR search returned five matching samples; the targeted result does not establish that such errors were absent.

likely_causes.title: Java heap exhaustion under high heap utilization
likely_causes.rationale: The 92% heap usage and GC overhead warnings, together with Java heap-space errors, support heap exhaustion as the immediate failure mode. They do not establish the underlying driver, such as a leak, workload change, or configuration issue.

supporting_evidence.detail: Seventeen WARN documents reported 'GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%' (version=v1.4.2); sampled occurrences span 2026-10-25T23:01:05+00:00 to 2026-10-26T00:17:05+00:00.
Five ERROR documents contained 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' (version=v1.4.2); sampled occurrences span 2026-10-25T23:55:05+00:00 to 2026-10-26T00:17:05+00:00.

next_steps: Collect a heap dump or allocation profile during high utilization to identify retained objects and allocation sources.
Review JVM heap configuration and GC telemetry, including allocation rates, post-GC heap levels, and pause behavior.
Check code, configuration, and deployment changes for checkout-service version v1.4.2.
Obtain workload and request-rate measurements before attributing the memory increase to traffic.
Correlate metric and log coverage to determine whether observations represent continuous behavior; the supplied samples do not prove continuous coverage or exact incident onset.
